slides.title: Discussing Future Plans
slides.content:
1. The 'Going To' Structure

In business, when we have a definite plan, we use:

Subject + AM/IS/ARE + GOING TO + Verb
  • I am going to hire a new assistant.
  • She is going to present the data.
  • We are going to open a new office.

2. Business Timeframes

  • Next Quarter (Q1, Q2...): The next 3-month period.
  • Upcoming: Happening soon (e.g., "The upcoming event").
  • Deadline: The final date to finish something.
slides.speech_text: When we talk about strategy, we don't usually guess. We have plans. We say: 'We are going to launch the product next quarter'. Don't forget the verb 'to be': I AM going to, She IS going to.

slides.title: Q3 Strategy Meeting
slides.content: Listen to the CEO discussing plans for the next quarter.
slides.audio_script:
CEO: Alright team, let's talk about Q3 (Quarter 3).
        Manager: What is the main goal?
        CEO: Well, we are going to expand into the Asian market.
        Manager: That's big. Who is going to lead that project?
        CEO: Sarah is going to travel to Tokyo next month to set it up.
        Manager: And what about the budget?
        CEO: The finance team is going to review it tomorrow.

quiz.question: What is the plan for Q3?
Who is going to travel to Tokyo?

questions.explanation: Siempre necesitas el verbo TO BE (am/is/are) antes de 'going to'.

options: I am not going to sign.
questions.explanation: La negación va en el verbo to be: 'I am NOT going to...'.

questions.text: Next month, the CEO _____ visit the factory.
questions.explanation: The CEO = He/She -> IS going to.

slides.title: Roleplay: Your Agenda
slides.system_prompt:
You are a manager asking an employee about their plans for next week.
        The user is the employee.
        
        Steps:
        1. Ask: "What are you going to do next week regarding the [Project Name]?"
        2. Ask specifically about a meeting or a deadline.
        3. End the conversation confirming the plan.
        
        Correction Focus: Ensure the user uses "I am going to..." instead of "I will..." or "I do...".
        If they say "I will call the client", say: "Since it's a plan, say 'I am going to call...'".
slides.initial_message: Let's review your schedule. What are you going to focus on next week?
slides.user_goal: State two planned actions using 'I am going to...'.
